newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Minorco seeks to boost Asia presence.
newsitem.headline: Minorco seeks to boost Asia presence.

text.p: South African-controlled, Luxembourg-listed resources group Minorco SA is in advanced talks on a number of mineral exploration alliances in South East Asia, a company official said on Wednesday.
Minorco on Tuesday announced a A$3.75 million agreement with Australia's Goldstream Mining NL, its first deal in the region since setting up an office in Singapore August.
Minorco's South East Asia managing director, Paul Cahill, told a briefing that Minorco was lagging competitors in the region since selling its stake in Australia's Normandy Mining Ltd in March 1996.
The Singapore office covers China to Australia, with the exception of Indonesia, Vietnam and Laos, where exploration is being pursued by an 50/50 joint venture with Normandy.
However, Cahill said Minorco was targetting Australia, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines and Malaysia, looking for gold deposits of more than 1.5 million ounces as well as copper, nickel and zinc.
An exploration manager has been appointed in Manila, and the group was in two sets of negotiations to take positions in exploration areas in the Philippines, he said.
Minorco is also in advanced discussions with a small Canadian explorer about farming in to two of its projects in the southern Highlands region of Papua New Guinea, he said.
The deals would be structured to keep Minorco's financial contribution down for the first two years while it decided if Papua New Guiea was suitable for "serious money".
"It's a sort of toe-in-the-water getting our feet dirty type of approach as we learn about the country," Cahill said.
He said Minorco had allocated US$8 million of its $55 million exploration budget to South East Asia this year, against $4 million out of $51 million last year.
Minorco sold its 18.9 percent stake in Normandy last year when the Australian company announced a four-way merger, which would have diluted Minorco's stake.
Minorco, which is controlled by South African giants De Beers and Anglo American, posted net earinings in calendar 1996 of US$396.4 million.
